rows.themeProjectDescription:
Project Description:

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely used in applications such as environmental monitoring, smart cities, underwater sensing, industrial automation, and disaster management. One of the major challenges in WSN deployment is achieving effective sensor coverage in complex and irregular environments containing obstacles such as buildings, terrain variations, or natural barriers. In many real-world scenarios, sensors are deployed randomly—using aerial distribution or autonomous systems—which can result in uneven coverage, blind spots, and unnecessary overlap between sensing regions. The presence of obstacles and irregular deployment boundaries makes coverage optimization more challenging, requiring intelligent strategies for sensor placement and network design. This project investigates the use of nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithms, an important subset of Artificial Intelligence (AI), including Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), to improve WSN coverage performance in realistic deployment environments. The project will develop simulation models to evaluate sensor coverage under different environmental conditions and obstacle configurations. A comparative study will then be conducted to analyze the performance of the selected optimization algorithms in terms of coverage quality, computational efficiency, robustness, and adaptability to irregular deployment spaces. The study aims to provide practical insights into selecting suitable optimization methods for large-scale and realistic WSN applications where environmental complexity significantly affects network performance. The project also offers students hands-on experience in simulation, optimization, and intelligent engineering system design using MATLAB.


Main Tasks:

1. Conduct a literature review on Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) coverage strategies, deployment challenges, and nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithms.

2. Develop simulation models to represent sensor node deployment in 2D spaces with obstacles, incorporating realistic environmental constraints.

3. Implement metaheuristic algorithms (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Ant Colony Optimization, and Grey Wolf Optimizer) for optimizing sensor placement.

4. Simulate and visualize sensor coverage, highlighting areas of blind spots, redundant overlap, and the impact of obstacles on signal propagation.

5. Evaluate and compare algorithm performance based on solution accuracy, robustness, computational efficiency, and ability to handle irregular and obstructed deployment zones.

6. Document the simulation model, algorithm implementation, experimental results, and analysis of findings.

7. Troubleshoot technical issues systematically using critical thinking and problem-solving skills.


Expected Results/Outcomes:

1. Develop functional simulation models that accurately reflect WSN coverage in complex deployment areas.

2. Identify the most effective metaheuristic algorithms for optimizing sensor placement under environmental constraints.

3. Produce visualizations and analyses demonstrating sensor coverage, obstacle effects, and deployment efficiency.

4. Enhance students’ skills in MATLAB simulation, optimization techniques, data analysis, and collaborative problem-solving.

5. Deliver a comprehensive report summarizing methodology, results, algorithm comparisons, and recommendations for practical WSN deployment.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background

Neuromorphic computing, which draws inspiration from the architecture and processing mechanisms of the human brain, has emerged as a promising paradigm to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck in conventional computing systems. At the heart of this technology lies the artificial synapse, a device that emulates the plasticity of biological synapses to enable efficient parallel, event-driven computation. Recently, optoelectronic synapses, which use light as the signal carrier, have attracted significant attention due to their potential for high bandwidth, low crosstalk, and ultrafast operation. Among the material candidates for such devices, perovskite materials stand out owing to their exceptional optoelectronic properties, including high absorption coefficients, long carrier diffusion lengths, tunable bandgaps, and defect tolerance. Furthermore, the unique mixed ionic-electronic conduction in perovskites can be harnessed to realize heterojunction-based devices that closely mimic short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity. The inherent interplay between photogenerated carriers and ion migration in perovskite heterojunctions provides a rich physical mechanism for tuning volatile and non-volatile photoresponses, making them ideal for constructing low-power, multifunctional optoelectronic synapses. This project is situated at the intersection of advanced materials science and neuromorphic engineering, aiming to explore the device physics of perovskite optoelectronic synapses and demonstrate their viability for neural network computation.


Main Task

1. The student is required to undertake a comprehensive study of the fundamentals of perovskite materials, with a specific focus on the working principles of the heterojunction structures that form the core of the synaptic device. This includes understanding charge generation, separation, and transport dynamics at the interface, as well as the key performance indicators such as responsivity, detectivity, response speed, and synaptic weight modulation.

2. The central experimental task involves learning the fabrication processes to prepare perovskite-based optoelectronic synaptic devices. After successful device fabrication, the student will systematically characterize their electrical and optical properties. A critical objective is to test and actively tune the devices’ volatile (short-term plasticity) and non-volatile (long-term potentiation/depression) characteristics by varying the parameters of the incident light pulses—such as intensity, duration, wavelength, and number of pulses—and by applying external bias. This step aims to establish the correlation between operational conditions and synaptic behavior.

3. Based on the experimentally extracted device dynamics, the student will use programming languages like Python to develop a simulation framework. This involves modeling the synaptic behavior and constructing a functional neural network, such as a feedforward or spiking neural network, to perform principle-level cognitive tasks like image recognition or pattern classification, thereby validating the device’s applicability in neuromorphic systems.


Expected Outcome

The anticipated outcomes of this graduation project encompass both hardware realization and software demonstration. On the hardware front, the project is expected to deliver a functional, principle-verifying perovskite optoelectronic synaptic device. Its volatile and non-volatile photoresponse will be thoroughly tested, analyzed, and documented. On the software side, a successful proof-of-concept neural network computation simulation, directly based on the measured characteristics of the fabricated device, will be implemented. This will demonstrate the device’s capability to serve as an artificial synapse for learning and memory tasks. The final deliverables will include a fabricated device sample, the associated simulation code, and a comprehensive written graduation thesis. The thesis will detail the perovskite material properties, device fabrication and characterization procedures, the tunable synaptic plasticity results, the neural network simulation methodology, and a critical analysis of the findings, thereby providing a complete account of the research from material to intelligent computation.
rows.themeTitle: Artificial synaptic devices and their applications in neuromorphic computing

With the development of new energy power generation, energy storage systems, and low-voltage DC power distribution technologies, the demand for supplying power to power-frequency AC loads from low-voltage DC sources is gradually increasing. This project will carry out a simulation study of a high step-up inverter circuit based on a cycloconverter, aimed at achieving a single-phase AC output of 220 V, 50 Hz, and 150 W under low-voltage DC input conditions of 25–40 V.

The tasks including:

1) learn the working principles of cycloconveter;

2) design and carry out simulation for the inverter in Matlab Simulink, including power stages and pwm generator.

rows.themeProjectDescription: A wireless communication system is designed for a V-shaped pipeline inspection robot to enable stable, low-latency bidirectional data transmission between the robot and the host computer as the robot moves through pipelines. The main research tasks include: overall system architecture design (communication frequency band selection, transmission protocol selection, antenna selection and layout); hardware circuit design for wireless communication (wireless module selection, baseband processing unit interface, power management); analysis of wireless signal propagation characteristics in pipeline environments and link budget evaluation; data encapsulation and communication protocol design (compressed image data transmission, command frame and control response mechanisms); and communication reliability enhancement strategies (packet retransmission, channel switching, error correction). Joint debugging of the wireless communication system with the V-shaped pipeline inspection robot is to be performed, followed by experimental validation of communication coverage, data rate, and stability in straight pipes, elbows, and long-distance pipeline environments.
rows.themeTitle: Design and Implementation of a Wireless Communication System for a V-Shaped Pipeline Inspection Robot
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription: A straightness measurement system is designed for pipeline inspection robots, enabling the robot to acquire real-time pipeline axis information while traveling along the inner pipe wall and to calculate pipeline straightness errors through data processing. The main research tasks include: overall system design of the straightness measurement system (measurement principle selection, sensor selection and configuration), hardware circuit design for data acquisition and processing (signal conditioning and acquisition of inertial measurement units, encoders, and displacement sensors), algorithms for pipeline axis fitting and straightness error calculation (least squares method, endpoint connection method), and calibration and error compensation techniques. Joint debugging of the measurement system with the pipeline inspection robot is to be performed, followed by experimental validation of straightness measurement accuracy and repeatability in pipeline environments.
rows.themeTitle: Design and Implementation of a Straightness Measurement System for Pipeline Inspection Robots
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription: A multi-camera-based circular structured light system is designed for three-dimensional measurement of pipeline inner walls. By synchronously capturing circular structured light fringe images from multiple cameras at different viewpoints, the system achieves high-precision reconstruction of the full panoramic inner wall profile. The main research tasks include: overall system architecture design (optimization of camera number and layout, ring laser selection and mounting, multi-camera synchronous triggering), calibration methods for the multi-camera system (intrinsic parameter calibration, joint extrinsic calibration across cameras, laser light plane calibration), multi-view image processing and fringe centerline extraction algorithms, and 3D point cloud reconstruction and stitching based on multi-view stereo matching. Joint debugging between the measurement system and the in-pipe robot is to be completed, followed by experimental validation of measurement accuracy, coverage range, and dynamic stability in typical pipeline environments.
rows.themeTitle: Design and Implementation of a Multi-View Circular Structured Light Measurement System for In-Pipe Robots
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription: A propulsion and pose measurement system for in-pipe robots is designed using a drag-chain-based propulsion scheme. The drag chain transmits driving force from an external power source to the robot body, allowing the robot to travel steadily in straight pipes of various diameters while acquiring real-time pose information. The main research tasks include: overall system design of the drag chain propulsion system (drag chain type selection, thrust transmission mechanism, routing and guiding methods); design of the pose measurement system (fusion of an inertial measurement unit and encoders, pipeline axis attitude calculation); design of the connection mechanism between the drag chain and the robot body; and hardware circuit design and integration (sensor signal acquisition, cable management inside the drag chain). Joint debugging of the propulsion and pose measurement system is to be performed, followed by experimental validation of propulsion stability and pose measurement accuracy in typical pipeline environments, including straight pipes of varying diameters.
rows.themeTitle: Design of a Drag-Chain-Based Propulsion and Pose Measurement System for In-Pipe Robots
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription: A monocular camera-based circular structured light system is designed to measure the inner wall profile of pipelines for a V-shaped inspection robot. The system enables the robot to acquire cross-sectional contour and morphological information while traveling through pipes of different diameters, elbows, and other complex geometries. The main research tasks include: overall system architecture design, hardware selection and integration of the camera and ring laser, development of image processing algorithms for circular structured light and laser stripe centerline extraction, and system calibration with error compensation methods. Joint debugging between the measurement system and the V-shaped robot is to be completed, followed by experimental validation of contour measurement accuracy and dynamic stability in typical pipeline environments including straight pipes, elbows, and variable-diameter sections.
rows.themeTitle: Design and Implementation of a Monocular Circular Structured Light Measurement System for a V-Shaped Pipeline Inspection Robot
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription: A V-shaped in-pipe robot is designed to accommodate varying pipe diameters, with the capability to autonomously navigate through elbows and inclined straight pipes. The robot is able to adapt to pipe shape changes without complex manipulation and can carry inspection payloads. The main research tasks include: overall mechanical structure design, hardware circuit design and integration, and control system development. A prototype is to be fabricated and subjected to software–hardware joint debugging, followed by passability and functional validation experiments in a long-distance pipeline environment.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Project Description:

This project focuses on the simulation and optimization of antenna placement in wireless communication systems using the free space propagation model. The model assumes ideal conditions—an environment without obstacles or reflective surfaces—allowing for simplified analysis of signal transmission between a transmitting and a receiving antenna. The aim is to analyze how distance, antenna gain, and signal frequency affect received signal strength, and to evaluate coverage performance over a defined area. A simulation environment will be developed using MATLAB to model signal propagation, visualize coverage, and assess the performance of different antenna configurations. To enhance the effectiveness of antenna deployment, the project will incorporate metaheuristic optimization algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) or Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). These methods will be used to determine optimal antenna placement strategies that maximize signal coverage or minimize power consumption. This study is relevant for applications in wireless communication planning, sensor networks, and radar systems, and contributes to the broader understanding of signal behavior and system design under ideal propagation conditions.


Expected Student Learning Outcomes:

1. Understanding of electromagnetic wave propagation in free space.

2. Application of mathematical models in antenna placement theory.

3. Simulation and visualization techniques using MATLAB.

4. Introduction to optimization techniques for engineering applications.

5. Experience in analyzing and interpreting signal coverage maps.

6. Applying basic project management skills, including task planning, time management, and progress tracking.

7. Maintaining project logs, writing technical reports, and effectively presenting research outcomes.

8. Collaborating effectively in teams across model development, programming, and data analysis tasks.

9. Addressing technical challenges through analytical thinking and systematic troubleshooting.


Expected Results/Outcomes:

1. Develop a functional MATLAB simulation model that accurately represents free-space signal propagation for antenna placement analysis.

2. Identify optimized antenna placement strategies using metaheuristic algorithms for improved signal coverage or reduced power consumption.

3. Gain insights into the relationship between antenna parameters, signal propagation, and coverage performance.

4. Provide a systematic evaluation and visualization of different antenna deployment scenarios.

5. Enhance student skills in MATLAB simulation, optimization techniques, data analysis, problem-solving, and technical reporting.

6. Deliver a comprehensive project report summarizing findings, methodologies, and recommendations for future antenna deployment studies.

PWM (pulse width modulation) signals are essential in power electronics. Nowadays, the frequency of PWM signals are pushing to mega-Hertz level which are difficult for general purpose MCU to generate.

The purpose of this project is to design a multi-channel PWM generator based on FPGA.

The specifications of the PWM generator are as follows:

1) 4 channel output, output 1 and output 2 are complementary and output 3 and output 4 are complementary;

2) frequency range: 10-20MHz;

3) deadtime adjustable within one output group;

4) phase could be adjusted between output 1 and output 3;

The student should take introductory analog and digital courses.
rows.themeTitle: Design of a multi-channel PWM Generator based on FPGA

Background: There are more than 27 million hearing-impaired people in China, they face communication barriers, while professional auxiliary devices are too expensive, and general AI cannot solve their exclusive pain points. We need to develop a low-cost edge-side communication assistant APP to help hearing-impaired people achieve barrier-free face-to-face communication.

Tasks:

1. Implement edge-side audio-visual fusion speech recognition, to improve recognition accuracy in noisy environments

2. Implement real-time sign language recognition, to complete the two-way communication closed loop

3. Develop an exclusive interactive interface, to adapt to the usage habits of hearing-impaired people

Work Content: Complete all development work independently, including mobile APP development, edge-side multimodal model optimization, sign language recognition fine-tuning and user testing. All work can be completed based on mature open source components, and all development can be finished within the undergraduate graduation project period.

Expected Outcomes: A complete mobile APP that supports Android system, as well as corresponding technical documents, user test reports and research reports.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) enables the transmission of data and power via the same electromagnetic (EM) wave. Given that both detection accuracy and energy harvesting efficiency at SWIPT receivers are proportional to the resource management and the coresponding equvalent signal to noise ratio, high-efficiency signal processing paradigm is required. 


The main tasks are including:

1) Investigate the principle of conventional SWIPT systems;

2) study the signal processing methods for typical SWIPT waveforms;

3) exploit efficient signal processing method for power-efficent SWIPT system;

4) evaluate system performace in terms of both BER and power harvest efficiency.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
For next generation wireless network，massive low-cost devices should be able to simultaneously connect to the same base station (BS) under severe constraints of spectral resources and power consumption. Therefore, further enhancement on both spectral efficiency (SE) and power efficiency (PE) is a primary target in the future mobile communications standards. Even though current multiple access techniques have a potential benefit to massive access compared to classical OFDMA, their power efficiency (PE) should be further considered especially for high-frequency channel with non-ideal power amplifier.

This work focuses on the waveform design in multicarrier-based OMA and NOMA communications:

1) investigate the performance of OFDMA and NOMA systems;

2) study the hybrid multiple access scheme on the trade-off between PE and SE;

﻿3) evaluate the performance of the multiple access systems with different multiuser detection schemes.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background


The rapid development of artificial intelligence has led to a surge in demand for efficient hardware acceleration solutions. While general-purpose processors handle control-intensive tasks well, they are often inefficient for compute-intensive neural network workloads. RISC-V, an open-source instruction set architecture, offers a unique opportunity for hardware customization and extensibility. This project aims to design a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) as a coprocessor tailored for neural network calculations, tightly coupled with a RISC-V core. The goal is to offload intensive arithmetic operations from the

main processor to achieve high performance and energy efficiency.


Main Tasks


● Architecture Design: Define the instruction set interface between the RISC-V core and the NPU coprocessor, including custom instructions for loading data, configuring parameters, and triggering computations.

● NPU Micro-architecture Implementation: Design and implement the internal architecture of the NPU, focusing on efficient data paths for matrix multiplication and convolution operations, potentially utilizing DSP and BRAM resources optimally.

● FPGA System Integration: Integrate the RISC-V soft-core processor with the custom NPU design on an FPGA development board, ensuring proper synchronization and data coherence.

● Verification and Testing: Develop testbenches and on-board test programs to validate the functionality of the accelerator using standard neural network models or representative computational kernels.


Expected Outcomes


● A complete Register-Transfer Level (RTL) design of the RISC-V NPU coprocessor system.

● A functional FPGA prototype capable of executing neural network inference tasks under the control of the RISC-V processor.

● Comprehensive performance evaluation metrics, including computational speedup compared to pure software execution, FPGA resource utilization (LUTs, FFs, DSPs, BRAMs), and system latency.

● A comparative analysis of the design's efficiency, demonstrating the advantages of hardware acceleration for specific AI workloads.
rows.themeTitle: Design and FPGA Implementation of a RISC-V NPU Coprocessor for Neural Network Computing

  • Familiarity with low-altitude airspace scenarios (UAVs, drones) and their channel characteristics (e.g., multipath, clutter, Doppler)

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Low-altitude airspace (e.g., below 300 meters) has become increasingly congested with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), drones, and other micro air vehicles. Reliable sensing of these targets is critical for air traffic control, security surveillance, and collision avoidance. Ground-based or infrastructure-mounted sensing base stations equipped with antenna arrays can perform passive or active beamforming to detect, localize, and track low-altitude targets. However, low-altitude sensing faces unique challenges: strong ground/sea clutter, multipath reflections, weak target radar cross-sections (RCS), and the need for real-time, high-precision angle measurement (both azimuth and elevation). Traditional beamforming and angle estimation algorithms (e.g., conventional delay-and-sum, Capon, MUSIC) often assume far-field, line-of-sight conditions, which may degrade severely in low-altitude environments with multipath and interference. This project aims to design dedicated beamforming strategies and novel angle measurement algorithms for low-altitude sensing base stations, ensuring robust detection and accurate angular localization of drones and other low-altitude targets under complex propagation conditions.

2. Main Task

  • Literature review: Review existing beamforming and AoA estimation methods for low-altitude sensing, including clutter suppression techniques (e.g., space-time adaptive processing, STAP) and super-resolution algorithms. Identify gaps: limited work on joint beam-domain processing for both azimuth and elevation, and few real-time solutions suitable for low-cost base stations.
  • System modeling:
  • Model a sensing base station equipped with a uniform planar array (UPA) or uniform linear array (ULA) operating in low-altitude scenarios.
  • Define the signal model including direct path, ground/sea reflections (multipath), and diffuse clutter.
  • Algorithm design:
  • Propose a robust beamforming scheme
  • Develop a high-resolution angle measurement algorithm specifically for low-altitude targets. This may involve:
  • 2D-MUSIC or 2D-ESPRIT for joint azimuth-elevation estimation.
  • Compressive sensing based sparse reconstruction, exploiting the sparsity of target angles in the vertical direction.
  • A deep learning based approach (e.g., a lightweight neural network) for fast AoA estimation under low SNR.
  • Design a processing pipeline: beamspace transformation (to reduce dimension) followed by angle estimation, optionally with recursive tracking for moving targets.
  • Simulation and validation: Implement the proposed algorithms in MATLAB. Simulate various low-altitude scenarios

3. Expected Outcomes

  • A well‑commented MATLAB code package implementing the beamforming and angle measurement modules.
  • A final technical report (40–50 pages) covering theoretical derivations, simulation results, and practical considerations (e.g., array calibration, mutual coupling effects).
rows.themeTitle: Research on Beamforming Design and Angle Measurement Algorithm for Low-Altitude Sensing Base Stations

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is the dominant waveform for modern communication systems (e.g., 4G/5G/Wi-Fi) due to its robustness against multipath fading and efficient frequency-domain equalization. Interestingly, OFDM also exhibits excellent properties for radar sensing: its wide bandwidth enables high range resolution, and the subcarrier structure allows flexible waveform design for joint range-Doppler estimation. Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) aims to unify both functions on a common hardware and spectrum resource. Using OFDM as the baseline waveform for ISAC is highly attractive because it is already widely deployed. However, conventional OFDM waveforms designed purely for communication may suffer from poor sensing performance (e.g., high sidelobes in the range-Doppler ambiguity function, power inefficiency for sensing). Conversely, radar-optimized OFDM waveforms may degrade communication bit-error-rate. This project focuses on designing novel OFDM-based ISAC waveforms and associated processing algorithms that jointly optimize communication throughput and sensing accuracy, with particular emphasis on low-complexity receivers and robustness to realistic channel impairments.

2. Main Task

  • Literature review: Survey existing OFDM-based ISAC schemes, including waveform parameter design (subcarrier spacing, guard intervals, pilot patterns), ambiguity function shaping, and joint communication-sensing processing.
  • Waveform and algorithm design:
  • Propose a flexible OFDM waveform parameterization (e.g., subcarrier weighting, null subcarrier insertion, or phase modulation across symbols) that balances communication and sensing performance.
  • Develop a joint optimization framework to minimize the range-Doppler sidelobe level under a communication rate constraint (or maximize rate under a sensing sidelobe constraint).
  • Design efficient processing algorithms at the receiver:
  • For sensing: 2D-FFT based range-Doppler processing, possibly with windowing or sparse recovery methods.
  • Optionally, incorporate adaptive waveform selection based on real-time channel feedback.
  • Simulation and comparison: Implement the proposed waveform and processing chain in MATLAB.

3. Expected Outcomes

  • A well-documented MATLAB/Python code package implementing the waveform generation, transmitter/receiver processing, and performance evaluation.
  • A final technical report (40–50 pages) covering literature review, methodology, numerical results, and recommendations for practical implementation (e.g., consideration of nonlinear amplifiers, phase noise).
  • Potential submission of a conference paper (e.g., IEEE Radar Conference or IEEE ICC) or an extended abstract.
rows.themeTitle: Research on Waveform Design and Processing Algorithm for OFDM-Based Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC)

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

In the domain of embedded systems and high-performance computing, the pipeline architecture serves as a cornerstone technique for enhancing processor throughput. By dividing the instruction execution cycle into distinct stages (typically Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory Access, and Write Back), a pipelined processor can overlap the processing of multiple instructions. This project focuses on the design and physical realization of a System-on-Chip (SOC) based on this classic RISC pipeline model, targeting deployment on FPGA hardware to validate real-world performance.

2. Main Tasks

The primary objectives of this project include:

● Architectural Design: Designing the datapath and control logic for a 5-stage pipeline, addressing hazards such as data dependencies and control stalls.

● SOC Integration: Integrating processor cores with on-chip memory (IMem/DMem) and basic peripherals to form a complete SOC.

● FPGA Implementation & Verification: Implementing the design on an FPGA development board, utilizing on-chip logic analyzers (e.g., ILA) for signal capture, and conducting rigorous functional and timing verification.

3. Expected Outcomes

Upon completion, the project should deliver:

● A fully functional RTL model of a 5-stage pipelined processor that passes simulation testbenches.

● A working FPGA prototype demonstrating the ability to execute a set of test instructions.

● A comprehensive technical report documenting the design flow, hazard resolution strategies, and performance analysis (e.g., clock frequency and instruction per cycle metrics).
rows.themeTitle: FPGA Implementation of a 5-Stage Pipelined SoC Architecture

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Spatial Modulation (SM) is a promising MIMO transmission technique that conveys information by activating different antenna indices, thereby reducing inter-channel interference and hardware complexity. Meanwhile, Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) has become a core paradigm for future wireless networks, where the same waveform and hardware are shared to achieve both high-rate communication and high-resolution sensing. Conventional ISAC beamforming designs often assume fully digital or hybrid architectures with amplitude/phase control on all antennas, which may be power-hungry and complex. By introducing spatial modulation into ISAC systems, one can exploit the antenna index domain not only for additional information bits but also for flexible beamsteering and sensing pattern control. However, the on–off nature of activated antennas in SM poses new challenges for beamforming design: the beam pattern must maintain low sidelobes and high angular resolution for sensing while ensuring reliable detection of the active antenna indices at the receiver. This project aims to develop novel beamforming and signal processing algorithms tailored for SM-based ISAC systems, enabling efficient joint design of communication and sensing functions.


2. Main Task

  • Literature review: Survey existing works on spatial modulation, hybrid beamforming for ISAC, and joint communication-sensing waveform design.
  • System modeling:
  • Establish a system model for an SM-ISAC downlink scenario: a transmitter with Nt antennas (only one or a subset active per time slot via spatial modulation) serving both a communication receiver (with index detection) and a sensing target (e.g., angle estimation).
  • Define performance metrics: achievable spectral efficiency (bps/Hz) and bit error rate (BER) for communication; beampattern matching error, Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for sensing.
  • Algorithm design:
  • Formulate an optimization problem that jointly designs the activated antenna indices and the analog/digital beamforming weights to minimize sensing beampattern distortion under a communication BER constraint (or maximize communication rate under a sensing CRB constraint).
  • Propose an iterative algorithm combining greedy antenna selection (for SM mapping) and manifold optimization for analog beamforming coefficients.
  • Optionally, design a low-complexity receiver that jointly decodes the spatial symbol and performs sensing parameter extraction.
  • Simulation and validation: Implement the proposed algorithms in MATLAB.


3. Expected Outcomes

  • A well-defined signal model and problem formulation for beamforming design in SM-ISAC systems.
  • A public MATLAB code package implementing the main algorithms and simulation scenarios.
  • A final technical report (40–50pages) covering literature review, methodology, numerical results, and future directions (e.g., extension to massive MIMO with reconfigurable intelligent surfaces).
rows.themeTitle: Research on Beamforming Design and Processing Algorithm for Integrated Sensing and Communication Based on Spatial Modulation

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for next-generation wireless networks (e.g., 6G), where the same hardware and spectrum resources are shared to perform both high-data-rate communication and high-resolution sensing (e.g., target detection, localization, and imaging). Hybrid beamforming, which combines a low-dimensional digital precoder with an analog phase-shifter network, offers a cost- and energy-efficient solution for large-scale MIMO systems. However, designing hybrid beamforming for ISAC systems faces challenges: the beamformer must simultaneously satisfy communication metrics (e.g., spectral efficiency, SINR) and sensing requirements (e.g., beampattern matching, Cramér–Rao bound). Most existing works treat the two functions separately or rely on fully digital architectures. This project aims to develop novel hybrid beamforming algorithms that jointly optimize both functionalities under hardware constraints.


2. Main Task

  • Literature review: Survey state-of-the-art hybrid beamforming designs for ISAC, identify research gaps (e.g., limited work on dynamic sensing-communication trade-off, phase shifter quantization effects).
  • System modeling: Establish a system model for a downlink ISAC transceiver with a partially connected or fully connected hybrid architecture. Define key performance indicators: achievable sum-rate for communication and beampattern matching error/clutter suppression for sensing.
  • Algorithm design:
  • Formulate a multi-objective optimization problem balancing communication and sensing metrics.
  • Propose an iterative algorithm based on alternating minimization or manifold optimization to solve the hybrid precoder/combiner.
  • Optionally, integrate deep unfolding or reinforcement learning for low-latency adaptation.
  • Simulation and analysis: Implement the proposed algorithm in MATLAB.


3. Expected Outcomes

  • A well-documented MATLAB code package and a final report (40–50 pages) summarizing the methodology, results, and future work.
rows.themeTitle: Research on Hybrid Beamforming Design Algorithm for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) Systems

rows.themeProjectDescription:
In modern industrial non-destructive testing (NDT), the accuracy of ultrasonic testing is constrained by the complex parameter combinations of the transmitting board. There exists a highly nonlinear coupling relationship among transmitting parameters such as Voltage, Frequency, Pulse Width, and Gate, Filtering, Backwall Echo, as well as Defect Echo. Conventional fixed-parameter testing methods struggle to cope with signal attenuation and noise interference under complex working conditions (e.g., small-diameter pipes, saddle-shaped welds).

This project aims to establish a mathematical model between the ultrasonic sound field and board parameters, and introduce the Spacetime Echo Potential (STEP) field theory to characterize the acoustic environment. Based on real-time acquired echo data, an intelligent control Agent employing an Actor-Critic architecture will be trained. The agent can dynamically optimize the transmitting board parameters according to the real-time feedback of echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and waveform characteristics, thereby achieving accurate defect identification and intelligent compensation, meeting the high demands for automation and intelligence in NDT for high-end manufacturing.
rows.themeTitle: Research and Development of an Intelligent Control Agent for Multi-channel Ultrasonic Testing System
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
